title: All Good Things

beats.what: Donna's anniversary party for Fatima establishes Colony House as a rare locus of warmth before the episode strips it away
Reverend confesses to Boyd that Sara is tied up in the church basement and lays out his full history -- the abused boy, the violent breakdown, the voice of God on the bridge
Boyd is shown the Reverend's buried bag with blood and recognises the logo; proof neither could have faked
Jade finds two pages stuck together in the yearbook, revealing new hidden drawings
A creature named Jasmine presses Kevin at the window; he lets her in, closing the window behind them
Creatures breach Colony House; chaos, casualties, Father Khatri mortally wounded on the steps
Victor leads Julie to a Farway Tree and pushes her inside; disappears -- destination unknown
Father Khatri dies; Boyd and Reverend pray the Lord's Prayer together over his body

character_beats.beat: Wants Boyd to accept Sara as an asset and take her on the forest journey; reveals his own catastrophic past to earn Boyd's trust even at the cost of admitting he broke town law
Wants to punish Sara and leave immediately; is persuaded to treat Sara as a map rather than a criminal when faced with the bag-logo evidence he cannot explain
Has been quietly preparing to leave; directs Julie into a Farway Tree for her safety then disappears rather than following, suggesting he is going somewhere intentional
Wants to maintain Colony House as a protected community; refuses to evacuate during the attack, stays to hold the line while the van departs without her

key_lines.line: I was the one who was supposed to listen.
key_lines.why: Reverend's confession pivot: his failure to listen to the boy is the wound that brought him here -- it mirrors Sara's function now

key_lines.line: Something was watching me that day, the same thing that told Sara
key_lines.why: Connects the bag-logo proof to the voices, establishing that whatever communicates with Sara also watched Boyd years before arrival
Reverend names the frame that justifies the entire forest expedition; Boyd's journey is recast as ordained, not desperate

key_lines.line: You have to find your brother. You have to warn him.
key_lines.why: Victor's instruction to Julie seeds a payoff arc that survives his disappearance -- her brother Ellis becomes the target warning

open_loops: Where does Victor go after pushing Julie into the Farway Tree, and why does he say it is starting?
What is in the yearbook's hidden stuck-together pages that Jade discovers?
Who is Jasmine -- one of the creatures -- and what does her ability to speak and feel loneliness imply about creature origin?
What was the Reverend meant to find at Colony House on the night God told him to get back in the car?
What is starting -- and what does Victor know about it that the other residents do not?

payoffs.what: The creature at the Reverend's door from E06's final shot is named Jasmine and shown speaking, feeling, and acting on loneliness -- confirming the creatures have interior lives
Boyd examines the drawing Sara produced in trance and recognises the logo on his buried bag, completing the proof loop that the voices have genuine knowledge

contradiction.wants: Absolution and a sanctioned path -- he wants Boyd to agree Sara is the key so his own rule-breaking becomes providence rather than crime
contradiction.does: Chains Sara in a basement, tells Boyd with a gun drawn, and openly admits he would rather Boyd shoot him than lose the chance to go home

tone_notes: The episode's single longest silence runs 99 seconds from 06:30 to 08:09 (minutes 6-7 register density 23, 0), entirely swallowing the title card and separating the pre-party setup from the party itself. This structural pause acts as a breath before the episode's densest sequence. Minutes 31-32 spike to 154 during the Boyd-Reverend negotiation, then plummet to 116/79 before the Colony House attack resets to 154 at minute 46 and peaks at 178 in the finale minute. The party-to-massacre arc is paced as a false plateau: minutes 8-25 cluster in the comfortable 80-133 range, lulling the viewer before the climactic crash.
